title: Animals
description: Animals grow and change through life cycles. Animals have body parts that help them survive. Some animals live in groups for protection and finding food.

exercises.question: A caterpillar changes into a ___.
exercises.exp: A caterpillar wraps itself in a chrysalis and transforms into a beautiful butterfly!

exercises.question: What is the correct order of a frog's life cycle?
exercises.exp: Frogs start as eggs, become tadpoles (with tails), then grow into adult frogs.

exercises.question: Which body part helps a BIRD fly?
exercises.exp: Wings help birds fly — feathers on the wings create lift and let birds soar!

exercises.question: Why do CARIBOU travel in large herds?
choices: for safety, warmth, and finding food
exercises.exp: Living in groups helps caribou stay safe from predators, share warmth, and find food.

exercises.question: A ruby-throated HUMMINGBIRD is a pollinator. What does it do?
choices: it carries pollen from flower to flower while drinking nectar
exercises.exp: Hummingbirds drink nectar from flowers and accidentally carry pollen between plants — they are pollinators!

exercises.question: What does a SEED DISPERSER do?
choices: it helps move seeds to new places so plants can grow
exercises.exp: Seed dispersers like squirrels and elephants carry seeds to new places where new plants can grow!

exercises.question: Why do LEAFCUTTER ANTS work together?
choices: to carry leaves too heavy for one ant to move
exercises.exp: Leafcutter ants form colonies and work together — each ant carries a leaf piece back to their underground garden.

exercises.question: What does a TADPOLE grow into?
exercises.exp: Tadpoles are baby frogs or toads — they live in water and slowly grow legs and lose their tail.

exercises.question: Which body part do FISH use to breathe underwater?
exercises.exp: Fish breathe through gills — they filter oxygen out of the water.

exercises.question: An AFRICAN ELEPHANT helps spread seeds by ___.
choices: eating fruit and dropping seeds far away in its dung
exercises.exp: Elephants eat fruit, travel far, and leave seeds in their dung — new plants can grow from these seeds!

exercises.question: What do AFRICAN WILD DOGS gain from hunting in a pack?
choices: they can catch prey too large for one dog to catch alone
exercises.exp: Hunting in packs lets wild dogs work together to bring down prey much larger than themselves.

exercises.question: Which is an example of an animal ADAPTING to its environment?
choices: a fish growing wings to fly
a polar bear having thick white fur to stay warm in the Arctic
a cat changing its colour every day
a bird swimming like a fish
exercises.exp: Polar bears have thick fur for warmth and white coats for camouflage in the snowy Arctic — perfect adaptations!

exercises.question: Which is the correct life cycle for a BUTTERFLY?
exercises.exp: Butterflies go through complete metamorphosis: egg → caterpillar (larva) → chrysalis (pupa) → butterfly (adult).

exercises.question: What do MIGRATORY birds do in the winter?
choices: they travel to warmer regions for food and warmth
they change their feathers to white
they eat extra food and stay in one place
exercises.exp: Many birds migrate — flying thousands of kilometres to warmer places where food is available during winter.

exercises.question: A BEAVER builds a DAM in a river. Why?
choices: to create a deep, still pond for their lodge home and food storage
to make the river flow faster
exercises.exp: Beavers build dams to create ponds — safe homes for their lodges and deep water to store food underwater for winter!

exercises.question: Which body part do KANGAROOS use to carry their babies?
exercises.exp: Kangaroos are marsupials — their babies (joeys) are born tiny and finish developing in the mother's warm belly pouch!

exercises.question: Why do GEESE fly in a V FORMATION during migration?
choices: the formation reduces air resistance — each goose benefits from the bird in front
they follow the leader by sight
exercises.exp: Flying in a V reduces drag for the birds behind — each goose gets a lift from the wingtip vortex of the one ahead. Smart teamwork!

exercises.question: A PAINTED LADY BUTTERFLY is a pollinator. When it visits a flower, it picks up pollen on ___.
choices: its body and legs as it feeds on nectar
exercises.exp: As a butterfly lands on a flower, pollen sticks to its fuzzy body and legs, then transfers to the next flower visited.

exercises.question: Which animal has the LONGEST migration — travelling up to 70,000 km per year?
exercises.exp: The Arctic tern migrates from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year — the longest migration of any animal!

exercises.question: What is HIBERNATION?
choices: a type of migration to warmer places
a deep sleep animals enter in winter to conserve energy when food is scarce
when animals change colour in winter
exercises.exp: Hibernating animals (like bears and groundhogs) sleep deeply all winter, living off stored fat when food is unavailable.

exercises.question: How do DEER communicate with each other?
choices: by tapping their hooves in patterns
using sounds (snorts, grunts), scent markings, and visual signals like tail flags
exercises.exp: Deer communicate using sounds, body language (raised white tail = danger!), and scent glands — a complex animal language.

exercises.question: A COMMON OSTRICH is the world's largest bird but cannot fly. How does it protect itself from predators?
choices: it can run at up to 70 km/h and delivers powerful kicks
it has venom in its beak
it changes colour to blend in
exercises.exp: Ostriches are the fastest running birds — sprinting at 70 km/h! Their powerful legs also deliver devastating kicks to predators.

exercises.question: Baby DUCKS follow their MOTHER as soon as they hatch. This behaviour is called ___.
exercises.exp: Imprinting is when baby animals bond with and follow the first moving creature they see after hatching — usually their mother!

exercises.question: Why do WOLVES HOWL?
choices: to communicate with their pack — marking territory, rallying members, and bonding
to scare away prey before hunting
exercises.exp: Wolf howls carry long distances and serve many purposes: rallying the pack, marking territory, and strengthening social bonds.

exercises.question: A mother CROCODILE carries her babies in her mouth to water. This is ___.
choices: a protective behaviour — she gently carries them safely to the water
exercises.exp: Crocodile mothers are surprisingly gentle with their babies! They carry them in their mouths to protect them.

exercises.question: Which animal is a HERBIVORE (plant-eater)?
exercises.exp: Giraffes eat only plants — mainly leaves from acacia trees that they reach with their incredibly long necks.

exercises.question: Which animal is a CARNIVORE (meat-eater)?
exercises.exp: Bald eagles are carnivores — they hunt fish, small mammals, and other birds with their powerful talons and hooked beak.

exercises.question: CAMOUFLAGE helps animals survive by ___.
choices: making them blend into their surroundings so predators (or prey) cannot see them easily
helping them find food by smell
exercises.exp: Camouflage is nature's disguise — animals with colours and patterns matching their habitat are harder to spot!

exercises.question: An AFRICAN WILD DOG's pups are cared for by the WHOLE PACK. This is an example of ___.
choices: cooperative group behaviour improving survival of young
the pups being ignored by adults
only the mother caring for young
exercises.exp: Wild dog packs cooperate to raise pups — adults share food (regurgitating it!), guard, and play with the pups. Pack parenting!

exercises.question: Which animal builds the MOST COMPLEX nest?
choices: a bald eagle (builds a massive stick nest called an eyrie)
exercises.exp: Bald eagles build enormous nests (eyries) in tall trees or on cliffs — adding to them each year until they can weigh over 900 kg!

exercises.question: A MONARCH BUTTERFLY migrates from Canada to Mexico — over 4,000 km. How do they know the way?
choices: they use a combination of the sun's position and Earth's magnetic field for navigation
older butterflies teach younger ones the route
they follow the smell of flowers
exercises.exp: Monarchs navigate using the sun as a compass and sensing Earth's magnetic field — incredible built-in navigation!

exercises.question: A butterfly starts as an egg, becomes a caterpillar, then a chrysalis, then a butterfly. This process is called ___.
exercises.exp: Metamorphosis is the dramatic change in body form during an animal's life cycle. Egg → Caterpillar → Chrysalis → Butterfly!

exercises.question: Frogs lay eggs in water. The eggs hatch into ___.
choices: tadpoles — which have tails and gills
exercises.exp: Frog eggs hatch into tadpoles — fish-like creatures with tails and gills. They gradually grow legs and lose their tails!

exercises.question: Which animal DOES NOT undergo complete metamorphosis?
exercises.exp: Grasshoppers undergo INCOMPLETE metamorphosis: egg → nymph (looks like small adult, no wings) → adult. No pupal/chrysalis stage!

exercises.question: A HERBIVORE is an animal that eats ___.
exercises.exp: Herbivores eat only plants — cows, rabbits, and horses are herbivores. They often have flat teeth for grinding plant material.

exercises.question: A CARNIVORE is an animal that eats ___.
exercises.exp: Carnivores eat meat (other animals) — lions, eagles, and sharks are carnivores. They often have sharp teeth or talons!

exercises.question: A BEAR eats berries, fish, honey, and small animals. A bear is an ___.
choices: omnivore — it eats both plants and animals
exercises.exp: Bears are omnivores — they eat almost anything available. Omni means 'all' in Latin. Humans are also omnivores!

exercises.question: What is a FOOD CHAIN?
choices: a chain store that sells food
a sequence showing how energy passes from one living thing to another through eating
a list of animals in order of size
the path food travels in the body
exercises.exp: A food chain shows who eats whom — and how energy flows from the sun through producers to consumers! For example: grass → rabbit → fox.

exercises.question: Which animal is at the START of most food chains?
choices: a large predator like a shark
exercises.exp: Food chains start with PRODUCERS — plants that capture the sun's energy. All animals trace their energy back to plants (or sunlight)!

exercises.question: A PREDATOR is an animal that ___.
choices: is hunted and killed by another animal
exercises.exp: A predator hunts and eats other animals (prey). Lions are predators of wildebeest. Predators help control prey populations.

exercises.question: A PREY animal is one that ___.
choices: is hunted and eaten by predators
exercises.exp: Prey animals are hunted by predators. Rabbits are prey for foxes. Many prey animals have adaptations to escape — camouflage, speed, warning colours.

exercises.question: NOCTURNAL animals are active ___.
exercises.exp: Nocturnal animals are active at night — like owls, bats, and hedgehogs. They have adapted eyes for seeing in the dark!

exercises.question: Which of these is an example of an ADAPTATION?
choices: a child learning to ride a bike
a polar bear's thick white fur coat helping it survive in the Arctic
exercises.exp: Adaptation is a heritable trait that helps an organism survive in its environment. Polar bear fur provides warmth AND camouflage!

exercises.question: Why do some animals HIBERNATE in winter?
choices: food is scarce in winter — hibernating saves energy until spring food returns
exercises.exp: Hibernation is a survival strategy — animals sleep deeply through winter when food is hard to find, living off stored fat.

exercises.question: Why do many birds FLY SOUTH in autumn?
choices: migration — they follow warmer temperatures and seasonal food supplies
exercises.exp: Migration follows food and warmth — birds fly to areas where insects, seeds, and fish are plentiful during their winter season.

exercises.question: An EXOSKELETON is ___.
choices: a skeleton inside the body (like ours)
a hard protective covering on the OUTSIDE of an animal's body
made of the same material as bone
exercises.exp: Insects, crabs, and lobsters have exoskeletons — hard shells on the outside that protect and support them. They shed it as they grow!

exercises.question: What happens to a caterpillar inside a chrysalis?
choices: its cells completely reorganise to form a butterfly — dramatic transformation
exercises.exp: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar's cells actually break down and completely reorganise into butterfly structures. Amazing metamorphosis!

exercises.question: How does a FISH breathe underwater?
choices: gills extract dissolved oxygen from the water
it comes to the surface for air every minute
exercises.exp: Fish have gills — specialized organs that extract dissolved oxygen from water as it flows over them. No lungs needed!

exercises.question: Which group of animals has DRY SCALY SKIN and lays eggs with leathery shells?
exercises.exp: Reptiles — like snakes, lizards, and turtles — have dry, scaly skin and lay leathery-shelled eggs, often on land.

exercises.question: Why do WHALES and DOLPHINS come to the surface regularly?
choices: to see where they are going
to eat fish at the surface
to breathe air — they are mammals with lungs, not gills
exercises.exp: Whales and dolphins are air-breathing mammals — they have lungs and must surface regularly to breathe through their blowholes!

exercises.question: A DECOMPOSER's role in a food chain is to ___.
choices: break down dead plants and animals, recycling nutrients back into the soil
exercises.exp: Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) break down dead matter — recycling nutrients back into the soil so plants can use them again!
